text:
talia: quick Q from the pricing block 12 
Are trial API keys throttled differently than paid keys, or do they just get lower monthly quotas?

ben: trials get both: slightly lower RPS/concurrency and smaller monthly token/embedding quotas. the idea is to avoid noisy zero-day spikes.

harper: follow-up: are embeddings and completion tokens drawn from the same quota pool? customers keep asking.

ben: theyre separate by default: tokens (generation) and embeddings tracked independently. we can create pooled promo credit accounts for specific customers if finance/sales opt in.

ops-bot: system: note - we already have a "soft cap" policy: soft cap = warning + grace; hard cap = reject. default grace window = 300s.

talia: what happens mid-request if quota hits? do we let the request finish or cut it off? need to set customer expectations.

harper: policy: in-flight requests are allowed to finish if they're under the grace window. if quota is exceeded outside grace -> 429/quota_exceeded. we try to avoid 402 during normal quota enforcement. 402 reserved for billing failure.

ben: error payload examples for SDKs (will add to docs):
```json
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "error": "quota_exceeded",
  "quota_type": "tokens",
  "grace_remaining": 120,
  "admin_url": "https://console.redwood.com/billing/org/ABC"
}
```

talia: nice. can we expose remaining quota programmatically so apps can show "X tokens left"? mobile team asked specifically.

harper: proposing an opt-in header plus a usage endpoint. header: `X-Redwood-Quota-Remaining: tokens=12345;embeddings=80` (only returned when the key owner enables it). endpoint: GET /v1/orgs/{org_id}/usage requires admin scope and returns detailed usage.

ben: security note: headers only on requests authenticated with a secret key belonging to the org; never on publicly embedded keys. we'll document RBAC for the usage endpoint.

talia: do promo credits ever automatically expand quota? sales wants a frictionless pilot experience.

billing-bot: system: promo credits reduce invoice balance by default. automatic credit->quota mapping is disabled. ops can apply a temporary quota top-up via a manual request (audit logged). were experimenting with a limited self-serve UI for vetted growth accounts.

harper: recommend: keep autopay/auto-topup opt-in. for pilots we can whitelist orgs for temporary quota increases but require sales & finance approval. audit trail is mandatory.

ben: webhooks - CS requested async alerts for quota thresholds. proposal: org.quota.threshold (payload: org_id, quota_type, percent_used, timestamp, admin_url) and org.quota.exceeded. these would be toggled per-org.

ops-bot: system: follow-ups created -> #7710 docs:quota-guidance, #7711 billing:promo-to-quota-policy, #7712 infra:usage-endpoint-auth

talia: last one: Dedicated customers - do they follow the same soft/grace policy? customers on Dedicated expect predictable behavior.

harper: Dedicated maps quotas to committed capacity in the contract. we still surface the same events and headers if enabled, but grace windows are shorter and SRE/solutions own emergency scaling.

ben: agreed. action items: docs will include the error payload examples + header opt-in guide; billing will outline the manual promo->quota flow; infra will spec the usage endpoint auth model.

all-hands-bot: Reminder: recording + slides uploaded to #all-hands; follow-ups #7710 #7711 #7712 created.

talia: thanks everyone, that clears a lot. will loop in CS and mobile on the follow-ups. :thumbsup:
